stem: A 25-year-old woman at 16 weeks of pregnancy feels well, with no palpitations, heat intolerance or cold intolerance. Her urine shows no protein and liver tests are normal. Her thyroid tests were normal a year ago, and they are repeated today.
oneliner: 25F + 16 weeks pregnant + feels well + normal liver tests, no proteinuria + thyroid tests normal last year → total T4, free T4, TSH?
ask: Which set of total T4, free T4 and TSH is expected?

whyNot.A: Raised free T4 with suppressed TSH is **thyrotoxicosis**; she has **no palpitations or heat intolerance**
whyNot.C: Low T4 with high TSH is **primary hypothyroidism**; she feels well with **no cold intolerance**
whyNot.D: Low total T4 is the **low binding-protein** pattern (nephrotic syndrome, liver failure); she has **no proteinuria** and **normal liver tests**, and is pregnant
whyNot.E: Raised free T4 with unsuppressed TSH means a **TSH-secreting** tumor or hormone resistance; she **feels well** and her tests were normal a year ago

answer: Total T4 up, free T4 and TSH unchanged
why: Estrogen of pregnancy makes the liver produce more **thyroxine-binding globulin**, so more T4 is bound and total T4 rises. The **free fraction** (under 1%) is what the pituitary senses, so free T4 and TSH stay **normal** and she remains euthyroid.
chain: Estrogen stimulates hepatic TBG synthesis
More circulating T4 is protein-bound
Total T4 rises
Free T4 stays normal after a brief dip
Pituitary senses normal free T4, so TSH stays normal

idea.rule: Total hormone follows the binding protein; free hormone and the feedback signal stay normal.
also: Oral contraceptive or estrogen therapy raises TBG and total T4
Nephrotic syndrome or androgens lower TBG: total T4 low, free T4 and TSH normal
Pregnancy raises corticosteroid-binding globulin: total cortisol up, free cortisol normal
Sex hormone-binding globulin changes alter total testosterone but not free

stem: A 5-year-old boy has a mutation that makes the calcium-sensing receptor active even without calcium bound. The receptor is found on parathyroid chief cells and on the basolateral side of thick ascending limb cells.
oneliner: 5M + gain-of-function calcium-sensing receptor mutation → serum calcium, PTH, urine calcium?
ask: Which set of serum calcium, PTH and urine calcium is expected?

whyNot.A: This is the **inactivating** mutation (familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia), the opposite of this boy's
whyNot.B: This is **vitamin D deficiency**, where PTH is high and urine calcium low; here the receptor is overactive
whyNot.D: This is **primary hyperparathyroidism**; his receptor signals falsely high calcium, not low
whyNot.E: High PTH with high urine calcium suggests **PTH resistance**; here PTH is switched **off** by the receptor

answer: Low calcium, low PTH, high urine calcium
why: An overactive receptor behaves as if calcium were **high**: the parathyroid cells **suppress PTH**, and the thick ascending limb stops reabsorbing calcium, so **urine calcium rises**. Serum calcium falls, and PTH stays inappropriately low.
chain: Receptor signals as though calcium is high
Chief cells reduce PTH release
Thick ascending limb stops reabsorbing calcium
Urine calcium rises, serum calcium falls

idea.rule: The calcium-sensing receptor reads serum calcium; activating mutation reads it too high (hypocalcemia), inactivating reads it too low (hypercalcemia).
also: Inactivating mutation (FHH): high calcium, low urine calcium, normal-high PTH
Cinacalcet activates the receptor to lower PTH in hyperparathyroidism
Lithium raises the receptor's set point, so calcium and PTH run higher

stem: A 43-year-old woman has a hoarse voice, cold intolerance and slow relaxation of her ankle reflexes. TSH and free T4 are both low. She is given a dose of TRH by injection, and TSH is measured again afterwards. TSH rises clearly.
oneliner: 43F + hoarse voice + slow reflex relaxation + low TSH and low T4 + TSH rises after TRH → where is the defect?
ask: Which level of the axis is at fault?

whyNot.A: A diseased pituitary would **fail** to raise TSH after TRH; hers responded
whyNot.C: Thyroid failure gives **high** TSH, not low
whyNot.D: Iodine deficiency also gives **high TSH** with goiter
whyNot.E: Resistance to thyroid hormone gives **high** TSH and T4, not low values

why: Low TSH with low T4 means the problem is **central**. A pituitary that can raise TSH when given TRH is working, so the defect is the **missing TRH** from the hypothalamus. No rise would localize the lesion to the pituitary.
chain: Hypothalamic TRH is deficient
Pituitary receives no stimulus, TSH falls
Thyroid makes less T4
Exogenous TRH restores TSH, showing a working pituitary

idea.rule: Low TSH with low T4 = central; TSH rise after TRH = hypothalamic, no rise = pituitary.
also: Primary hypothyroidism: high TSH, low T4 (feedback intact)
Sheehan syndrome or a pituitary macroadenoma: TSH fails to rise after TRH
CRH stimulation: ACTH rises in hypothalamic but not pituitary ACTH deficiency

stem: In an experiment, a healthy volunteer receives intravenous insulin and blood is sampled at the glucose nadir. Plasma epinephrine has risen about 20-fold from baseline, while plasma norepinephrine has risen less than 2-fold.
oneliner: Experiment: healthy volunteer + IV insulin hypoglycemia + epinephrine up 20-fold, norepinephrine under 2-fold → why?
ask: Which is the best explanation for the larger epinephrine response?

options.A: Reuptake of norepinephrine into sympathetic nerve endings
options.C: Failure of monoamine oxidase to metabolize epinephrine
options.E: Selective stimulation of the adrenal medulla

whyNot.A: Reuptake limits norepinephrine spillover in **every** sympathetic response; it does not explain why this stimulus gives an **epinephrine-dominant** rise
whyNot.B: COMT **degrades** catecholamines; it would not raise epinephrine selectively
whyNot.C: Both hormones share the same metabolic enzymes, so this cannot explain **only** epinephrine
whyNot.D: Both have similarly short half-lives, so stability does not account for the **gap**

answer: Selective activation of the adrenal medulla
why: Hypoglycemia is sensed centrally and drives a **selective adrenomedullary** response: the adrenal medulla secretes mostly **epinephrine** straight into the blood. Sympathetic nerve outflow, the main source of plasma norepinephrine, rises much less, so the catecholamine pattern depends on **which arm the stressor activates**, not on differences in clearance.
chain: Low glucose is sensed by hypothalamic and brainstem glucose sensors
Preganglionic output to the adrenal medulla rises sharply
Chromaffin cells release mainly epinephrine into the blood
Sympathetic nerve outflow rises far less, so norepinephrine rises only slightly

idea.rule: Stressors activate the sympathoadrenal system selectively; hypoglycemia drives mainly adrenal medullary epinephrine.
also: Standing up and cold exposure raise mainly norepinephrine from sympathetic nerves
The adrenal medulla makes about 80% epinephrine because PNMT is induced by cortisol from the cortex
Hypoglycemia unawareness in long-standing type 1 diabetes reflects a blunted adrenomedullary epinephrine response

stem: In an experiment, a healthy man has urine flow, urine osmolality and serum osmolality measured every 30 minutes after an injection at time zero. Urine flow falls from 3 to 1 mL/min, urine osmolality rises, and serum osmolality drifts slightly lower.
oneliner: Experiment: healthy man + urine flow 3→1 mL/min + urine osm up + serum osm down after injection → which substance?
ask: Which substance was most likely injected?

whyNot.A: Aldosterone retains **sodium** and wastes potassium, with little effect on urine flow or serum dilution
whyNot.B: ANP **raises** sodium and water excretion, so flow would go up
whyNot.C: A loop diuretic **increases** urine flow with isosmotic urine
whyNot.E: Mannitol is an osmotic diuretic: flow **rises**

why: Falling flow with **more concentrated urine** and a lower serum osmolality means the collecting duct is **reabsorbing water**: ADH inserts aquaporin-2 channels, retaining free water that dilutes the blood.
chain: ADH binds V2 receptors on principal cells
Aquaporin-2 channels are inserted
Water leaves the tubule, urine concentrates, flow falls
Water enters plasma and lowers serum osmolality

idea.rule: ADH: free water retained, urine flow down, urine osmolality up, serum osmolality down.
also: Absent ADH (central DI): large dilute urine, high serum osmolality
SIADH is the pathologic version of this response
Diuretics and osmotic agents raise urine flow
Aquaporin-2 inserts via V2 receptor and cAMP
